how: We read the website of every Indianapolis wedding florist listed on Lazo (109 listings, 92 sites reachable) and set aside the ones that are not really in the wedding business: flower preservation studios, same-day delivery and gift shops, a tea room, a studio with placeholder text still on its site, and planners and venues listed as florists. What is left is a shortlist of vendors who say clearly what they do, show their work, and tell you how they work. Verified Lazo vendors come first. Nobody paid to be here, and this is not a ranking: Lazo ranks only on reviews from couples who booked.
ask: Do you design and install at the venue, or deliver arrangements? Installation and teardown are the price difference.
What is grown in Indiana for my month, and what has to be shipped in, especially for a winter or early-spring wedding?
Can I see a full wedding's florals at a budget like mine, not a single bouquet photo?

picks.name: Duet Floral Studio
picks.blurb: A team of wedding and event designers in a Fountain Square studio who have flowered over 200 events in the Midwest and beyond, with work published in Style Me Pretty and Wedding Day Magazine and featured on Fox 59. Duet puts a budget calculator on its site so you get an estimated range before the first call.

picks.name: A Bride's Choice Florist
picks.blurb: Deborah Summers grew up in her parents' flower shop and brings over 25 years in floral and 16 years running her own business, with work featured in professional publications and at Newfields Art in Bloom. The site lays out the design process step by step.

picks.name: One of a Kind Events
picks.blurb: Floral design treated as art, from ceilings cascading with flowers to small vases on a cocktail table, with a stated commitment to the highest quality product and a no-negativity team. One of a Kind starts every design by collaborating with the couple on the exact look and feeling.

picks.name: Flora + Flame
picks.blurb: Bespoke floral design for weddings and events in Indianapolis, from custom large-scale installations to smaller curated florals. Flora + Flame builds its process to be collaborative and stress-free from the first concept to the final installation.

picks.name: Camino & Company
picks.blurb: A mobile flower shop and wedding studio run by Karly with local flower farmers, locally sourced blooms and her grandpa's 1984 El Camino. Camino & Company blends vintage, old-fashioned vibes with modern floral design, out of Noblesville.

picks.name: K.I.S Florals
picks.blurb: Powered by JPS Events, the operator of the Regions Tower venue, and built on over 18 years of floral installations for its in-house weddings. K.I.S says floral is not its only revenue source, which it argues changes how it can price custom work, and everything can be ordered online.

picks.name: Accent Floral Design LLC
picks.blurb: Three decades in the flower field, starting as a designer for a hotel floral shop on Maui, where the work ran to avant-garde projects on a grand scale, before moving back to the mainland and into weddings. Accent Floral Design is based in Zionsville.

picks.name: the Archivist
picks.blurb: Paula Shoultz is a multidisciplinary artist who has practiced flower design for weddings and events since 2007 and runs the practice without floral foam to cut waste. She also photographs weddings in a photojournalistic style, so one artist could cover both.

picks.name: N Bloom
picks.blurb: A wedding and event florist in Mooresville with a second base in Clearwater, Florida, specializing in event design and what it calls floralscapes. Nicole's team designs the once-in-a-lifetime pieces alongside the couple so the flowers match the event's character.

picks.name: Frida's Flowers
picks.blurb: A wedding and event floral artist whose work puts rich culture, vibrant color and beauty at the center, under the banner Flores y Cultura. Frida's Flowers is an Indianapolis studio for couples who want color and culture in the flowers.

picks.name: Lily Ever After | Floral Arch Rentals
picks.blurb: Not fresh flowers: Lily Ever After rents real-touch faux floral arches, aisle flowers and flower walls across Indianapolis and Carmel, pitched as the cost, waste and unpredictability of fresh stems removed. Hand-curated packages cover the ceremony and reception.

picks.name: Farm Stand
picks.blurb: For DIY couples: a Noblesville flower farm growing ranunculus, peonies, stock, sweet peas, lisianthus and more from March through late October, selling DIY event buckets and wholesale blooms as well as bouquets. Sweet Peas also runs a farm stand, The Bloomery, and u-pick days.
